notes.text: Quinn Hughes is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Yakov Trenin is away for personal reasons and missed their last game. Nico Sturm has taken his spot beside Danila Yurov and Maxim Shabanov.
Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin.
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, down from 34% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 53:03 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Kiefer Sherwood is out week to week (upper body injury) and missed their last game.
Alexander Wennberg returned in their last game after missing 2 games.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the NHL with 38 points, the Sharks fourth in the Pacific with 22 points.

SJS.head: The Sharks face a real test
SJS.body: Even though Minnesota may be without Hughes and San Jose has home-ice advantage, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Celebrini’s favorite opponent
paras: The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Minnesota on Nov 6. The Sharks (10-12-2) lost 5-2 to Calgary on Tuesday. The Wild are on a tear, five straight wins. Going in, the Wild are first in the NHL and the Sharks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 20th in the NHL).

The Wild’s record (.792) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.636), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Sharks’ (.458 on chances worth .399), largely thanks to their goaltending.
In their five-game winning streak, the Wild have outscored teams 24-9, including 16-7 at 5-on-5.

The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks. On top of that, both teams like to hit, especially the Sharks (2nd), so expect plenty of it.

Kirill Kaprizov (18 G / 25 A / 43 P in 24 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games and eight goals in nine games against San Jose since 2023-24. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (9 G / 18 A / 27 P in 22 GP), who has a point in seven straight games against Minnesota. Will Smith (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 24 GP) is next in line.
Jesper Wallstedt (16-2-3 / .925 SV% in 21 GS) has been terrific for Minnesota and will likely start. Yaroslav Askarov (6-9-1 / .888 SV% in 16 GS) is in line to start for San Jose.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: The Wild are newly without Quinn Hughes, Yakov Trenin and Olli Määttä, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche are missing more right now.
The Sharks are newly without Kiefer Sherwood, and have been without Igor Chernyshov since Oct 22.
Kirill Kaprizov has a point in 13 straight games.
Maxim Shabanov has nine goals on chances worth about 5.3 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
